transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I’m here because for the past year, I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. No matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine... I know the chart doesn’t match what I saw. I just know it. And honestly, dealing with it is just really wearing me down.
Would you say that most people would agree with your belief about the lab results being changed or held back?

No, they definitely don't agree. Like I said, I've had doctors, nurses, even my own family tell me the numbers are fine and that I'm wrong. But I'm a phlebotomist, I draw blood and look at these kinds of things all the time. I know what I saw originally, and the chart they have now just... it doesn't match. It's been a whole year of me trying to prove that someone in the system is altering or hiding parts of his results. Nobody believes me, but I know I'm right, and it's just really wearing me down trying to get someone to listen.
Would you describe the idea that someone is changing or holding back your dad's lab results as something that most people would consider unusual or hard to believe?

Yeah, I mean... I guess most people do think it's unusual. They look at me like I'm crazy when I try to explain it to them. They just trust the system and the doctors completely, so the idea that someone would actually go in and mess with a patient's chart... it's hard for them to swallow. But just because it's hard to believe doesn't mean it isn't happening. I know what I saw.
Have you ever had a period of time where you didn't believe someone was changing or holding back your dad's lab results?

No, not since this all started a year ago. Once I saw that the numbers didn't match, I've known for a fact that someone is tampering with them. There hasn't been a single day or... any period of time where I thought I was wrong or just stopped believing it. I know what I saw, so it's just been a constant reality for me this whole time.
Has this belief about your dad's lab results affected your relationships or daily activities in any way?

Yeah, it has. My family... they've actually started leaving me out of some of the planning for his appointments because I keep bringing it up and they don't want to hear it. And at work, it's affecting things too. I really feel like I'm no longer being considered for lab supervision. People there seem to think I make record issues too confrontational now, just because I'm so focused on making sure everything is accurate after what happened with my dad's chart. So, yes, it's definitely impacting my life.
Do you think it's possible that you might be mistaken about the lab results?

No, I really don't think I'm mistaken. I mean, I'm a phlebotomist, I work around this stuff every day. For the past year, I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. And no matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine, I know the chart doesn’t match what I saw. I know it. But honestly... constantly trying to get people to see the truth, it’s really wearing me down.
Would you say that the idea someone is altering your dad's lab results is something that could happen in real life?

Yes, of course it can. I mean, I work in the medical field, so I use these electronic record systems every single day. Anyone with the right administrative access can go in and alter a value, or just hide a specific test result from the main view. It's not impossible at all. It's just a matter of logging in and changing the data. So yes, it's definitely something that can happen in real life, which is why I know that's what is happening with my dad's chart.
Do you think there's any evidence that could change your mind about someone altering your dad's lab results?

No, I don't think so. I mean, like I said, for the past year I've been trying to prove this. I know what I saw. Every time a doctor or my family tells me the numbers are fine, it doesn't change anything because I know the chart doesn't match what was originally there. I know someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of his results. It doesn't matter what anyone says at this point. Honestly, just... constantly having to defend this, it's really wearing me down. But no, I can't think of any evidence that would make me unsee what I saw.
Would you describe the idea that someone is changing or holding back your dad's lab results as something that could happen to anyone, or is it specifically targeted at your dad or your family?

I don't know if it's specifically targeted at us, or if they do it to other people too. I haven't really looked into other patients' charts, you know? I just know what's happening with my dad. It could be that someone has a personal issue with him, or maybe it's just a corrupt system and we're caught in it. I'm just focused on his results.
How does the idea that someone is changing or holding back your dad's lab results seem to you in terms of being unusual or strange?

I don't really think it's strange at all. I mean... people do unethical things every day, right? And like I said before, I work with these systems. It's just data. Someone logging in and hiding a file or changing a number isn't some crazy, impossible thing. It's actually pretty basic. So, no, I don't see it as unusual. It's just exactly what is happening to him.
Do you think the reason someone would be changing your dad's lab results is something that makes sense to you, or is it something that doesn't have a clear explanation?

I'm not really sure, honestly. I don't have a clear explanation for the "why." 

I mean... I know it's happening, but I don't know exactly what the motive is. Maybe someone made a mistake with his bloodwork and they're just trying to cover their tracks? I don't know. I haven't figured that part out. I just know what the numbers were originally, and I know they've been changed. The actual reason behind it is... well, it's something I'm still trying to understand.
Do you think the people changing your dad's lab results are doing it in a organized or systematic way?

I'm not really sure. I haven't seen anything that points to it being... you know, a big organized effort or anything like that. I just know what I saw in his specific file. Whether it's just one person doing it on their own or some larger system... I really don't know. I haven't looked into it that far, so I couldn't tell you if it's systematic.
Has there ever been a moment, even if briefly, where you doubted your belief that someone is changing or holding back your dad's lab results?

No. Honestly, no, I haven't doubted it. I'm here because for the past year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. And no matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine, I know what I saw. I know the chart doesn’t match what I originally looked at. It’s just... it's really wearing me down, having everyone tell me I'm wrong when I know I'm not. But no, I haven't doubted it, because I know what the numbers were.
Has your belief that someone is changing or holding back your dad's lab results ever wavered, even for a short time?

Like I just said, no, it hasn't wavered at all. I've been at this for a year now, trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of his results. It doesn't matter how many doctors or family members try to tell me his numbers are fine. I know the chart doesn't match what I originally saw. It's just... it's really wearing me down having to constantly defend it to everyone, but I know what I saw. So no, I haven't doubted it for a second.
Is there anything that could potentially change your belief about your dad's lab results being altered?

No. I don't think anything could change my mind. I've spent the last year trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is altering or hiding parts of his results. It doesn't matter how many doctors or family members tell me his numbers are fine, or try to show me printouts. I know what I saw originally, and I know the chart doesn't match it. It's exhausting, honestly, having everyone tell me I'm wrong when I know I'm right, but no... nothing is going to make me unsee what I saw.
Do you think your belief about your dad's lab results is based on facts or is it just a feeling you have?

It's based on facts. It's not just some feeling. I feel like I'm repeating myself, but I'm here because for the past year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s results. I saw the original numbers. So no matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine now, I know the chart doesn’t match what I saw. That's a fact. It’s just... it's really wearing me down that no one else will just look at the facts.
Is it possible for you to imagine any situation where you might be wrong about the lab results?

No, it's not possible. I know I'm not wrong. Like I've been saying, I'm here because for the past year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. It doesn't matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine. I know the chart doesn’t match what I saw. It’s just... it’s wearing me down that I have to keep explaining this. I saw what I saw.
How much time would you say you spend each day thinking about your dad's lab results and trying to prove your point?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't exactly timed it or kept track of the hours. It's just... it's on my mind most of the time. When I'm not at work, I'm usually looking through the papers I have or trying to figure out what happened in the system, but I couldn't give you a specific amount of time that it takes up each day.
Do you think your belief about your dad's lab results would change if you were shown conclusive evidence that the charts have not been altered?

No, I don't think it would. Because... well, I know I keep saying this, but any evidence you pull from that system is exactly what I've spent the last year trying to prove has been altered. Someone inside the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of his results. 

So, no matter how many doctors or family members bring me these so-called conclusive charts and tell me the numbers are fine... I know they don't match what I originally saw. It's just really wearing me down to keep having to defend this when I know what's actually happening.
